skill.name: marketing-ideas
skill.description: Generates and prioritizes SaaS marketing ideas from a 139-tactic catalog using product stage, audience, budget, resources, timeline, and growth goals.
skill.summary: Find practical SaaS growth ideas matched to your goals, stage, budget, and team.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: All ten static findings are false positives. Nine entries describe paid marketing or numbered idea ranges, while the remaining entry uses Markdown backticks around filenames rather than shell execution. The catalog separately recommends cross-company remarketing audience sharing without consent, policy, or governance safeguards.

remediation.issue: Cross-company remarketing audience sharing can expose personal data and violate consent or platform rules.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the tactic or require documented consent, approved data processing, minimization, and compliance review before any audience sharing.

content.value_statement: SaaS teams often struggle to choose relevant growth tactics from too many options. This skill filters 139 ideas by stage, budget, audience, timeline, and goal.
actual_capabilities: Selects three to five ideas based on product, audience, stage, budget, team size, and timeline.
Draws recommendations from a catalog of 139 tactics across 17 marketing categories.
Explains why each idea fits, how to begin, expected outcomes, and required resources.
Prioritizes tactics for fast leads, authority, low-budget growth, product-led growth, and enterprise sales.
Routes detailed channel execution to related specialist skills when appropriate.
limitations: Provides strategic recommendations, not automatic campaign execution or performance measurement.
Relies on user-provided context and optional local product marketing documents.
Does not verify current channel costs, platform policies, legal requirements, or market conditions.
Detailed referral, email, advertising, and SEO implementation may require related specialist skills.

use_cases.title: Prioritize bootstrapped growth
use_cases.description: Choose affordable tactics for an early-stage SaaS product with limited budget, time, and staff.

use_cases.title: Generate enterprise leads
use_cases.description: Compare paid, outbound, partnership, and authority tactics for a defined enterprise audience and monthly budget.

use_cases.title: Build category authority
use_cases.description: Identify research, content, speaking, and media ideas that strengthen recognition in a specialized market.

prompt_templates.title: Get starter ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest five marketing ideas for [product] serving [audience]. My stage is [stage], budget is [budget], and goal is [goal].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a short, relevant starting list.

prompt_templates.title: Compare low-budget options
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend three marketing tactics that avoid paid advertising for [product]. Rank them by expected impact, effort, and time to results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when spending is limited and prioritization matters.

prompt_templates.title: Design a growth portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a balanced marketing portfolio for [product] with [team size] and [monthly budget]. Include one quick win, one medium-term tactic, and one compounding tactic.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when balancing immediate demand with durable growth.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate and sequence tactics
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate our context: [context]. Select five tactics for [goal]. Score fit, effort, cost, speed, and risk. Recommend testing order and success indicators.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when previous results and operating constraints are available.

output_examples.input: We sell e-commerce analytics, have 200 customers, three employees, and a monthly marketing budget of $500.
output: Easy Keyword Ranking: Target overlooked e-commerce analytics searches. Validate customer language, assess difficulty, and publish three focused pages.
Integration Marketing: Partner with complementary commerce tools. Select one shared audience, propose a joint webinar, and track qualified signups.
Founder Welcome Email: Add a personal message after signup. Explain the core outcome, invite replies, and measure activation.

output_examples.input: We need faster leads for enterprise security software and can spend $10,000 monthly.
output: Google Ads: Capture high-intent category searches. Start with narrow keywords and dedicated landing pages. Expect faster learning with controlled spend.
LinkedIn Ads: Target security leaders by role and company size. Test two offers and measure qualified meetings.
Conference Sponsorship: Select events with verified buyer attendance. Negotiate speaking access and measure conversations, meetings, and pipeline.

best_practices: Provide product, audience, stage, budget, team size, timeline, and one measurable growth goal.
Request three to five ideas when you need depth, prioritization, and concrete starting steps.
Share previous results so recommendations can avoid failed tactics and build on proven channels.
anti_patterns: Do not request a large unfiltered list when resources or goals are unclear.
Do not treat expected outcomes as forecasts without validating assumptions through small tests.
Do not use the catalog as legal, privacy, platform-policy, or compliance guidance.

faq.question: Which products does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on SaaS and software products across pre-launch, early, growth, and scale stages.

faq.question: How many ideas does it recommend?
faq.answer: It normally recommends three to five focused ideas, but it can provide a broader categorized list.

faq.question: Can it create a complete marketing plan?
faq.answer: It provides selected tactics and starting steps. Use a dedicated marketing planning skill for a comprehensive plan.

faq.question: Does it execute campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It recommends strategies and implementation steps but does not launch advertisements, emails, events, or integrations.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your product, audience, stage, budget, team, timeline, goal, and previous marketing results.

faq.question: Are the recommendations always current?
faq.answer: No. Verify current costs, policies, laws, and platform availability before implementing any tactic.
